reden: Yes. The audit report explicitly flags that eq() performs a raw bitwise equality (packedFloat.unwrap(a) == packedFloat.unwrap(b)), which fails when two numerically equal values are encoded differently as M vs L (due to the L flag and multiple encodings from toPackedFloat/divL). This matches H-04 exactly: same function (Float128.eq), same root cause (raw word compare ignoring L_MANTISSA_FLAG/normalization), same impact (eq returns false for equal values), and the same remedy (normalize/scale/decode before comparing). Fixing the audit’s issue would fix H-04.
